en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-guhyasamāja-mahātantrarāja-sūtra*, Scroll One. Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta,
Imperially Appointed Court Honorable of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Recipient of the Purple Robe, together with others, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.

Thus have I heard: At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in the great celestial palace of Śakra, within the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, on the ground adorned with various soft ornaments. He was accompanied by a great assembly of bodhisattvas numbering one hundred and sixty million koṭis of nayutas—namely:

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrāṅkuśa, the Bodhisattva [Vajra... (Note: The provided source text appears to be truncated. The translation reflects the portion available.)
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Cāpa, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrasādhu, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajragarbha,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajraprabha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajradhvaja, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrarati, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajranetra.
[Sarva-]vajra Wisdom Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Vajra Turning of the Wheel of Dharma Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva,
Vajra Speech Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Vajra Action Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva,
Vajra Diligence Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, and Vajra Subduer of Māras Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Vajramuṣṭi and others; furthermore, the four thousand Vajra-vidyārājñīs, including Vajralāsyā, Vajramālā, Vajragītā, and Vajranṛtyā;
and further, Vajrāṅkuśī, Vajrapāśī, Vajrasphoṭā, and Vajraghaṇṭā...
...and the assembly of the four thousand Vajra Attendants, as well as the assembly of the four thousand Vajra Goddess Attendants, including Vajragandhā, Vajrapuṣpā, Vajradīpā,
and Vajrānulepanā; furthermore, there were the assemblies of Mahābrahmā, Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, and others.
Together with Śakra, Lord of Devas, and his retinue, as well as countless koṭis of celestial maidens from that heaven who,
having conceived hearts of joy, played exquisite music and collectively performed the most supreme and vast offerings.

At that time, the great maṇḍala assembly of those devas extended for a thousand yojanas; the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, was situated within it, surrounded by a respectful retinue of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of beings who were listening to and receiving his teaching of the Dharma.

At that time, the Great Lord of Secrets, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi—the Great Vajradhara—surveyed the entire assembly within the gathering. With his left hand, he formed the *vajra-utkṣepa-mudrā* (the seal of the raised vajra), and with his right hand, he playfully brandished the primordial, wondrous, great *vajra* of bliss, placing it at his heart center in a posture of heroic valor. He then spoke this secret heart-mantra of the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas:

When this heart-mantra "HŪṂ" was uttered, all worlds shook universally; all Tathāgatas once again realized perfect enlightenment through the great bodhi-wisdom of all Buddhas; and the indestructible activity of benefiting all sentient beings was brought to ultimate fulfillment by all Bodhisattvas. Śakra, Lord of Devas, together with his retinue, all came to abide in the samādhi of the accomplishment of Vajrasattva.

At that time, when the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, had likewise manifested the realization of perfect enlightenment, all the Tathāgatas together exhorted the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"May you bring about great benefit and happiness for all sentient beings and cause them to achieve accomplishment in all secret dharmas; you should now proclaim the supreme ultimate meaning of the purity of all dharmas and the most sublime secret dharma-meaning of your own family."

At that time, having heard the exhortations of all the Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi first performed the vajra-snap of the fingers and then spoke the heart-mantra for summoning all the Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ mahāsukhavajrasattva sarvatathāgatānugṛhīta praveśasamayadhṛk vaśīkuru śīghraṃ mīmāmaha-maṇḍalapanna jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. When this great mantra was spoken, all the Tathāgatas of all worlds in the ten directions gathered like clouds, filling the entirety of space like sesame seeds with no gaps between them.
At that time, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya resided before the World-Honored One, surrounded by four bodhisattvas, including Vajrapāṇi;
the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava resided to the right of the World-Honored One, surrounded by four bodhisattvas, including Vajragarbha;
and the Tathāgata Avalokiteśvararāja resided behind the World-Honored One, surrounded by four bodhisattvas, including Vajranetra.
To the left of the World-Honored One dwells the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi of the North, surrounded by the four bodhisattvas beginning with Vajrakarma;
each of these Tathāgatas abides established in their respective hand-symbols (mudrās).

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having universally gathered the entire assembly of the Tathāgata’s great congregation and even all worlds, causing them all to dwell securely within the Great Maṇḍala of the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, spoke this secret vajra song of the vidyā-mantra and performed the rite of secret offering.
The respective great vidyās are as follows:
*vajrasattva saṃgraha* (1) *vajraratna* (2) *mānottara* (3) *vajradharma gāyana* (4) *vajrakarma kuru bhava* (5) Furthermore, the mantra for the maṇḍala is proclaimed:
"I shall now proclaim according to the dharma The Great Vajradhātu Maṇḍala."
The equality of that Vajradhātu is what is called the Vajradhātu.
Once the site of the maṇḍala has been purified, one should be embraced by the great mudrā of the deity.
Having observed this universally, one performs the accomplishment through countless recitations.
The maṇḍala has the appearance of four sides, with four gates and four shrines well-arranged;
according to the ritual, that altar site is constructed with a length and breadth of thirty-three cubits.
At the four gates and four corners, one performs the *nīrūha*;
the center is adorned with silk banners, and furthermore, the shape of a crescent moon is established, embellished with vajra-jewels.
According to the ritual, one should draw four pavilions, well-arranged in their center;
opening the mandala gates according to the Vajra-dharma, the four Vajra-gates and so forth are opened.
Opening the door, he spoke clearly:
"Within the mandala, one should draw an eight-spoked wheel; using vajra-thread, perform the measurements, beginning first from the north and proceeding in sequence.
With four lines of measurement, mark the positions for the human wheels."
Within that wheel, according to the root ritual manual, one should arrange the images of the five directional Buddhas;
on the spokes and corners to the left and right of the five Buddhas, one should paint the figures of those performing play, garlands, song, and dance.
In the four corners of the maṇḍala, one should paint the deities of Incense, Flower, Lamp, and Ointment, as well as the four Vidyārājas—
Aṅkuśa, Pāśa, Śṛṅkhalā, and Ghaṇṭā— in the southeast, south, west, and north gates, respectively.
Having thus arranged these Buddhas, worthy ones, and sages according to the ritual,
and having completed the vajra maṇḍala through drawing with colored powders, one should then summon all the worthy ones and sages.
The mantra for summoning is as follows:
"When this great mantra is thus spoken, all the supreme Buddhas and the assembly of devaputras present in the gathering shall all enter the dharma of Vajrasattva."
Next, there appear auspicious signs such as joy, or celestial light, or exquisite fragrances;
whether one sees them for oneself or others do so as well, those who behold these auspicious omens shall attain the most supreme [attainment].
Having attained the supreme samādhi, one is embraced by Vajrapāṇi and the others;
first seeking accomplishment through a single gate, one proceeds sequentially with the hook, lasso, chain, and bell.
All offerings and secret offerings should be presented according to the ritual with exquisite flowers and the like;
fill the auspicious vase with various fragrant waters, insert a vajra branch, and perform the recitation.
When this Great Illumination is thus proclaimed, all mudrās and samayas of the Supreme Vajrasattva and others,
as well as the rites of offering and so forth, shall all be entered.
If one drinks that nectar-water, or sprinkles it for purification according to the ritual,
one's physical form, strength, life-span, and well-being will be restored and strengthened, and one will be able to accomplish all feats of siddhi.
Thereafter, according to one's capacity, cause the disciple to cover their face with clean white cloth and don a red robe;
lead them into the maṇḍala according to the ritual, first having them cast flowers and subsequently making secret offerings.
Having entered, first receive the vajra-mudrā; next, grant the samaya-vow and admonish them, saying:
"If you break the samaya of Vajrapāṇi, this vajra shall shatter your crown."
The Great Illumination says:
"Thereafter, look up at the altar above; holding a sublime flower, cast it as you wish.
Wherever the flower falls is the primary deity (iṣṭadevatā). Thereafter, seek the method for supreme accomplishment."
Next, one should remove the cloth covering the face and prostrate with the entire body cast upon the ground;
having paid homage to the principal deity of the maṇḍala, one presents secret offerings such as the playful dance;
having clearly beheld the appearance of the maṇḍala, one realizes the assembly of all sentient beings.
Contemplating that which has already occurred according to the ritual of empowerment, one sprinkles the crown of the head with vajra water and displays the five-wisdom vajra,
as well as the great vajra and so forth, according to the ritual.
Having thus bestowed their respective insignia, one should then establish them by means of vajra names;
for all great beings such as Vajrapāṇi and others are born from the vajra-mind.
Having bestowed the Vajra-secret mudrā and taught the Dharma of the Amoghasamaya, one should not be separated from Vajrasattva; from him all Tathāgatas are born.
According to the ritual, at the time of early dawn, one should recite the name of the Vajra Honored One once, and then bestow the Vajra Precepts:
"Vajrapāṇi is your supreme honored one; this vajra is the Great Vajra. May you always achieve whatever you desire."
Thereafter, one again presents the secret offerings, universally making offerings to the supreme maṇḍala,
presenting all manner of offering substances such as exquisite flowers according to one's preference.
"This is called the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
Furthermore, among all the methods for accomplishment (*sādhana*), the method for the accomplishment of the body is explained first:

if a practitioner wishes to create an image of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi—whether by casting, carving, molding, or painting—they should fashion it according to their preference and in accordance with the ritual rules, and then arrange solemn offerings before that image."

The practitioner, wearing red garments and forming the Vajra-utkṣepa mudrā, should focus single-mindedly on the recitation for one year without limiting the number of repetitions. Even regarding all desired foods, drinks, and pleasures, he may enjoy them as he wishes, meeting with no obstacles whatsoever.
After one full year has passed, his practice will be perfected, and he shall attain the state of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi in this very life.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishing speech is proclaimed as follows:

the practitioner, according to the ritual, at any place and at any time, should recite with vajra-speech a limit of one hundred thousand times. Once the count is complete, he shall obtain all the accomplishments bestowed by all the Tathāgatas; in his second birth, he shall immediately attain Buddhahood, and thereafter he will certainly become the Honored One Vajrapāṇi.
"Furthermore, the method for accomplishing the mind is proclaimed:

the practitioner, according to the ritual, at any place and at any time, performs the secret internal visualization and recitation in accordance with their intention. Having completed four months, they shall immediately attain the supreme accomplishment as desired, and all activities performed in this present life will be successful."
"Furthermore, the method for accomplishing the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi is proclaimed:

The practitioner, according to the ritual, stands before an image of the deity, forms a vajra-fist with the left hand and holds a vajra with the right hand. Having recited the mantra one hundred thousand times according to the ritual, one immediately attains the accomplishment of the vajra."

Having grasped this vajra, one may come and go at will and act with sovereign mastery and unimpeded freedom in all desired activities. Furthermore, one shall attain the presence of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and all the Tathāgatas—whether appearing hidden or manifest—to accomplish the rites of siddhi. According to one's desires, these practitioners shall be granted transformations and enjoyments, and all other undertakings shall be brought to complete fulfillment. Moreover, in this very life, they shall achieve the state of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
"Furthermore, regarding the general method for accomplishing the three types of action:

the practitioner should, according to the ritual procedures of the root text, install the honored image in any suitable place at any suitable time. Before that image, one should bind the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and, while clearly visualizing the deity, perform recitation for one year."
When the period has expired, one shall become the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
Furthermore, regarding the detailed exposition of the various methods for accomplishment:

the practitioner should perform recitation in accordance with the ritual of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi; thereby, they will further attain all supreme dharmas of resolve and the accomplishment of all matters, behold the body of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, and hear his words:
"Day by day, one shall attain all accomplishments.

One should know that regarding this secret dharma-gate of Vajrasattva, even if one is unable to accomplish the aforementioned methods, merely entering this maṇḍala will enable one to effectively perform all forms of protection, pacify calamities for peace and happiness, increase longevity, enhance physical appearance and vitality, provide strength and diligence, grant heroic majesty, and augment virtuous dharmas.

All various illnesses such as malarial poisons, the suffering and distress of grief, evil dreams and ill omens, possession by *ḍākinīs* and other spirits, all obstacles—namely the obstacles of phenomena (*dharmāvaraṇa*), the obstacles of karma (*karmāvaraṇa*), and the obstacles of afflictions (*kleśāvaraṇa*)—premature death, all fears, all unwholesome dharmas, and all other forms of suffering, can be extinguished.

Furthermore, one is able to perform acts such as *āveśa* (possession), causing [beings] to tremble, or performing song and dance; or speaking of future events, manifesting bodily forms, or producing sounds; or performing subjugation and destruction, or concealment and restraint; or binding by means of mudrās and mantras, or inducing confusion; or binding, or releasing; or being able to summon all that is desired, even universally summoning all the world, causing them all to be possessed (*āveśa*) and to practice loving devotion.

"Regarding such matters as these, one attains mastery and is able to perform all activities; one achieves the three vajra-karmas of all things, manifests all illusory transformations and other phenomena, and can alter the passage of time and destroy dwellings. All the *kiṃkaras*, yakṣas, piśācas, and their various retinues are brought under complete control. Furthermore, one can restrain all wind, rain, lightning, and thunderbolts; one can summon timely, sweet rains; one can uproot and destroy forests and their fruits and flowers; and one can cause flowers and fruits to grow out of season."

In brief, all matters—whether hidden or manifest, rising or sinking, and those pertaining to benefit and so forth—are accomplished according to one's wishes; even all the most supreme methods of accomplishment are fully perfected.
Therefore, one should know that this secret heart-mantra of Vajrasattva and its maṇḍala are capable of performing the aforementioned hundredfold activities.
All that has been explained above constitutes the secret dharma-gate of Vajrasattva.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, together with all the Tathāgatas, laughed joyfully and in unison proclaimed the Vidyā-mantra of the Vajra of the Manifestly Realized Enlightenment-Wisdom of All Tathāgatas, saying:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgatamātike mahāsukhavajradhāriṇi | sarvasamantapracaṇḍe | sarvanokavikṣepagari | sarvasukhapraṇayike | sarvārthasādhani svāhā. Having spoken this great mantra, all the Tathāgatas addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying: "Vajrapāṇi!"
"You should receive and uphold this great vidyā-mantra of mine to bring great benefit to all sentient beings.
I shall now proclaim the maṇḍala rite:

the practitioner should, according to the ritual procedures of the root text, draw an outer maṇḍala in a square shape using colored powders; in its center, one should fashion an eight-spoked wheel, and upon the hub of the wheel place Vairocana Tathāgata, while on the eight positions of the spokes, one should paint the eight Tathāgatas."

Having duly laid out the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then binds the fist-mudrā of all Tathāgatas, dons the appropriate garments, enters the maṇḍala, and prostrates his entire body upon the ground in worship of the noble deities.
First, recite the mantra for invocation as follows:

“Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajraghoṣe mahācakreśvari sarvadharmaprabhāsani sarvasamādhimudrāni sarvapūjāvidhivistarākarṣaya vadhaya svāhā. Having recited this great mantra, all the Tathāgatas and the various sages and deities will gather like clouds, manifesting auspicious signs such as joy and other such portents.
Thereafter, the ācārya instructs the disciple to dress as before, covers his face with a clean white cloth, and, forming vajra-añjali and holding a beautiful flower, leads him into the maṇḍala.
Having entered, one should be granted these verses of samādhi:
"One should know that the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha Is the supreme and most excellent refuge;
One should constantly make offerings to them for as long as life lasts, And should not offer worship to other deities."
"Furthermore, he bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, saying:

'Oṃ hana vajra narakāśa sakaho. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then removed the face-cloth and immediately had the disciple prostrate himself fully upon the ground to pay homage to the noble ones."

Next, one should bestow the great vajra, followed by the consecration with the five vases of the Tathāgata, as well as the transmission of the vidyā-mantra of the respective family and instruction in the mudrās; thereafter, one should perform offerings according to one's capacity and exit the maṇḍala.
"This is called the Great Dhāraṇī Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for its accomplishment is proclaimed as follows:

The practitioner should sit cross-legged before an image of the Tathāgata according to the ritual procedures of this teaching, bind the Fist Seal of all Tathāgatas, and recite the mantra for one year without limiting the number of repetitions. Eating only once a day, one should do nothing else and must not give rise to weariness or discouragement, as prescribed in the original teaching."

After one year has passed, he shall immediately attain Buddhahood, becoming the sovereign lord of all the three realms; dwelling eternally with mastery, his lifespan shall be immeasurable, and he will skillfully tame and transform the realms of all sentient beings.

Regarding the methods for accomplishment as explained above, even if a practitioner has not yet attained success, they should simply recite this great mantra with a mind of focused attention; they will likewise be able to accomplish all undertakings—namely, first attaining the fivefold merit, and eventually performing various activities such as turning the wheel of Dharma and delivering sentient beings—and thereafter, before long, they shall also attain Buddhahood.
"This is called the Great Dhāraṇī Ritual of All Tathāgatas.
At that time, during the Great Ritual Assembly for the Destruction of Evil by Vajra, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi again addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:

"May you please uphold this Great Samaya of the Great Mantra Ritual, the Secret Heart-Mantra for the Destruction of Evil by Vajra. It shall subdue all evil ones, as well as all other beings such as devas who give rise to wrathful, malicious, and perverse thoughts toward the teachings of the Tathāgatas; it shall cause them all to fall [from their ways], so that from the moment they were first subdued at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), no further evils may arise."
At that time, all the Tathāgatas remained silent.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi—desiring to fulfill all supreme vows—bound the *vajra-utkṣepa-mudrā* with his left hand, brandished the vajra playfully with his right hand, and with a joyful smile, sat in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and spoke this secret heart-mantra:
“Oṃ niḥsvabhāvātmaka vaṃ vajra hūṃ phaṭ. When he spoke this heart-mantra, all worlds shook throughout their entirety.

Furthermore, all Tathāgatas, through the great bodhi-wisdom of all Buddhas, manifest the realization of perfect enlightenment; they cause all mountain crags to collapse and fall apart, and they thoroughly subdue all malevolent beings. Universally summoning them, they cause them all to enter the maṇḍala, where they abide in samādhi and perform acts of loving-kindness.

All hosts of mātṛkā spirits, bhūtas, malefic planets, yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśācas, yakṣas, and so forth—even those belonging to the realms of hell—are utterly shattered and destroyed, crying out in confusion.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, having subdued all beings as required for their conversion, surveyed everywhere with his vajra-eye. He manifested the Great Wrathful Honored One Vajra Trailokyavijaya and his retinue of wrathful deities, who possessed extremely fierce and malevolent features, bared fangs and bit their lips, and knit their brows. They were surrounded by a great, blazing mass of fiery light and held vajra-hooks, khaṭvāṅgas, swords, nooses, tridents, staffs, bells, banners, and other such implements, further adorned with various kinds of ornaments.
Having thus appeared, they stood surrounding the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi spoke this ritual procedure for the Trailokyavijaya Great Maṇḍala:
“First, one should act in accordance with the ritual applications of that Great Maṇḍala; next, one should draw this outer maṇḍala, making it perfectly complete in form.”
The Inner Vajra Maṇḍala is fashioned in a square shape;

in its center is placed the Great Vajradhara Lord Vajrapāṇi, his face manifesting both wrathful and joyful expressions, with sharp fangs protruding outward. His left hand forms the *vajrotkṣepa-mudrā* or holds a blue lotus, while his right hand playfully hurls a vajra.
In front is placed the Great Wrathful Deity Vajra Trailokyavijaya.
To the right, place the Vajra Hook Wrathful Deity;
behind, place the Vajra Sword Deity;
and to the left, place the Vajra Lasso Deity.
In its four corners, one should paint the wrathful Vajra Lords: Vajrakāla, Vajradaṇḍa, and Vajramurunda.

Having thus completed the painting, the Vajrācārya, dressed in blue garments and forming the Trailokyavijaya mudrā, assumes a wrathful expression and enters the maṇḍala. After prostrating to the noble deities, he recites this verse:
"For the benefit of all sentient beings, For the sake of accomplishing all teachings, And for the extensive subduing of wicked multitudes, May Vajrasattva empower me."
"Then, one should form the Vajrāṅkuśa mudrā: with the two hands, slightly bend the tips of the index fingers so that they resemble a hook to form the seal.
Recite this great mantra of invocation: Oṃ raṇi-sambhava-vajra-grasaya praveśaya. (1) (2)
PAMDHAYA SVĀŚIRU MAHĀVJRA DHĀRMANĀYA HŪṂ.
6. SARVA-VAJRA-KURANA-KARṢAYA HŪṂ 7. SARVA-MĀRĀ-GAṆA-PRAVEŚAYA HŪṂ 8. SARVA-SAMAYĀMUDRANAYA HŪṂ

*Sarvakarmasiddhiṇy amoghapratiṣṭhānasādhye hūṃ hūṃ jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ jaḥ.* (9) “If this great vidyā-mantra is recited twenty-one times, all the Vajradhara vidyā-queens will enter into the Vajrasattva of the Vajra Family of all Tathāgatas. (10)
At that time, the Vajrācārya assumes a wrathful form, causing all beings to attain *āveśa*, whereby all obstacles and all transgressions are completely extinguished.

The ācārya then again assumes a wrathful form, binds the vajra-striking mudrā, and presents various offerings. Thereafter, he causes the disciple to likewise don a blue robe and have his face covered with blue silk; the disciple also assumes a wrathful form, first binds the vajra-striking mudrā, and next should hold a flower.
Having led them into the maṇḍala, he bestowed this samaya verse:
"For the benefit of all sentient beings, To subdue all who are most wicked,
Every day at the break of dawn, One should cast the vajra once in a circular motion."
"Furthermore, he confers this great vidyā, saying:
'Oṃ niḥsvabhāvavajra hūṃ phaṭ. Having conferred this great vidyā, the disciple then casts a flower; the place where the flower falls is that of the tutelary deity."
Afterwards, remove the face-cloth. Once the disciple has prostrated before the noble deities, they should cast the vajra.
Next, one should confer the vajra initiation and instruct them in the heart-mantra and the methods of mudrā. Having performed offerings according to their preference, they may exit the maṇḍala.
"This is called the Vajra Trailokyavijaya Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

the practitioner should fashion a painted image (paṭa) according to the ritual procedures of this very teaching; in the center, one should paint the wrathful vidyārāja Vajra Trailokyavijaya, on the right side one should paint four wrathful kings, and on the left side likewise one should paint four wrathful kings."
Having painted it in this manner, one should install it according to the ritual rules.

The practitioner, before that image, casts a vajra, sits in the full lotus posture (paryaṅka), assumes a wrathful expression and a wrathful gaze, and recites the mantra one hundred thousand times. Once the prescribed number is completed, he shall cause his own body to become like that of the Great Vajra Wrathful King; all his physical appearance, lifespan, power, and diligence will be entirely equal [to his], and he will likewise be endowed with supernatural powers (abhijñā), enlightened activities (karma), and the methods for great accomplishment (mahāsiddhi), benefiting sentient beings without end.

"If one has not yet achieved the aforementioned accomplishments, merely by entering this maṇḍala and reciting the great vidyā-mantra once as described above, one can perform a hundred kinds of activities. That is to say:

among all evils pertaining to both sentient and non-sentient beings, one can completely restrain them; cause their destruction and terrify them; demolish, conceal, and delude them; bind, disperse, sever, and bring them into disorder."

Furthermore, it can cause various malevolent sentient beings to either utter speech or remain silent; to be driven away or coerced; to become servants; to be obstructed from seeing; to be possessed by malaria; to sink into the earth; or to fall into the hells (*naraka*) or be reborn among the animals (*tiryagyoni*). It can even prohibit worldly *puruṣasiddhi* (human accomplishments), causing all harmonious matters to become discordant, and subsequently instigating acts of opposition and harm.

Furthermore, by means of other conditions, they can manifest signs such as playful laughter; they can both cause illness and cure illness, even to the point of causing all malevolent beings to perish.
Furthermore, one is able to summon all beings, causing them to enter into possession (*āveśa*) and perform acts of loving devotion.
As for those who should be subdued, one may cause them to tremble, dance, sing, laugh, and jest, or cause them to extensively proclaim matters concerning the future and so forth.
In this way, all who are evil shall be made to respect, love, and be subdued; all undertakings shall be brought to completion;

If any practitioners cultivate this dharma, they will be able to sever all afflictions and sufferings, and attain the accomplishment of sublime bliss.”
The mantra syllables of the wheel-gate are as follows:
"Akāru-mukhaṃ sarvadharmāṇām ānunnatānta. When this mantra syllable-wheel was spoken, all sentient beings were completely able to sever and eliminate the suffering of all afflictions.
The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī spoke again: "Vajrapāṇi!

If there are people who daily recite and contemplate these gateways of syllables and these verses of equality, they shall all completely sever all obstacles and the suffering of afflictions, and they shall not be invaded or harassed by any evil Māras due to their causal conditions."

If one recites this Dharma-gate of the syllable-wheel, it is equivalent to reciting and upholding the Prajñāpāramitā and so forth; it universally gathers all the incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Dharma-gates of the Mahāyāna secret seals, swiftly brings about the attainment of the fruit of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and ensures that all supreme methods of accomplishment according to one’s heart’s desire are fully realized.
Furthermore, regarding the exposition of this maṇḍala ritual:

according to the rules, one first draws the outer maṇḍala; in its center, one further constructs that wheel of syllables—the wheel of syllables refers to the letter *A* and so forth—with all the letters pervading within that wheel. One installs the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, holding a vajra-sword and manifesting the aspect of subjugating all Tathāgatas.
In the four cardinal directions and four intermediate corners, draw the eight Bodhisattvas of Liberation, each holding a Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra and each in the posture of entering samādhi.

Once the powder drawings have been completed in this manner, the Vajrācārya then bares his right shoulder, forms the Vajra-sword mudrā, and enters the maṇḍala. Placing his kneecaps on the ground, he prostrates to the noble deities.

With both hands forming the vajra-bind, the two middle fingers curved like hooks, he performs the invocation mudrā and recites this great vidyā-mantra for invoking all the noble deities: Oṃ sarvatathāgataniṣpannāya hīḥ. (1)

Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity descends, manifesting red-colored flames that blaze forth everywhere, capable of bestowing the accomplishment of all that is desired.

Having entered, the *ācārya* imparts this samaya verse, saying:
"This adamantine arrow of great compassion now Shatters all your feelings of aversion and weariness."
"Furthermore, this Vajra-Wisdom Bow shall cause you to be free from craving, attachment, and pride.

Afterward, he confers the mudrās and the empowerment of the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā) of the respective family as before, and subsequently confers the Great Vajra-Arrow.

Furthermore, he should be given the name Vajramahāprema. Thereafter, the disciple should perform vajra-dance and vajra-song as an offering, whether throughout the entire night or until midnight; one must not sleep, but may freely enjoy songs, dances, and various foods and drinks as desired.
In this manner, for one month or even for a year, one should not sleep, but should perform all the rites of accomplishment according to the Dharma.
Thereafter, having obtained all wealth and happiness, all that is desired, and all offerings, one may then, as appropriate, exit the maṇḍala.
"Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed as follows:
the practitioner should fashion an image of the Bodhisattva Vajrācāpa from red wood and bind the mudrā of the Vajra Arrow."

Having performed this, the practitioner shall recite the mantra according to the ritual for one year; thereafter, they will attain the state of the Bodhisattva Vajracāpa, with infinite lifespan, neither aging nor dying.

"Regarding those who have not yet achieved what has been described above, if they can recite this great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) of this very family even once, they will likewise attain the power of attraction, summoning, and *āveśa* (possession); or they may cause [beings] to dance, sing, and laugh at will; or they may dispatch demons, release, bind, or seize wealth; or they may cause all defiled states such as greed, hatred, and delusion to increase or to cease; or they may increase auspicious and wholesome qualities, bring about delight and joy, and effect attraction; furthermore, they shall achieve success in all objects of sensory pleasure, including form, fragrance, taste, and touch."
“This is called the Great Ritual Manual of the King of Tantras of the Great Samaya, the Vajra of Universal Adoration.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Rājavikrīḍita addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

“I shall now also proclaim within this great ritual manual of yours a Dharma gate that is excellent. If there are practitioners who cultivate this Dharma, those persons will always receive the praise of all Tathāgatas; how much more so would there be others who do not praise them?”

Furthermore, if a practitioner recites "sādhū sādhū" one thousand times daily before Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva or a Tathāgata—or without limit in number—this person will attain purity of mind and receive the extensive praise of all Tathāgatas, who will constantly and without interruption exclaim, "Excellent! Excellent! All methods for attaining accomplishments (*siddhi*) will then be successfully realized.
"Furthermore, the ritual procedure for this maṇḍala is explained:

According to the rules, one should draw the outer maṇḍala; within it, the inner maṇḍala shall have four sides and four gates, with the Bodhisattva Vajrasādhu installed at the center. On the four sides and four corners, the eight noble beings of the Vajrasādhus are to be installed."
Having thus laid out the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms the vajra-sādhu-muṣṭi mudrā, enters the maṇḍala, and, assuming the gesture of "well done" (sādhu), prostrates to the noble deities.
First, recite *sādu sādu*. Next, with both hands, slightly bend the tips of the index fingers like hooks to form the mudrā of invocation.

Recite this mantra of invocation: *Oṃ vajra-ḍṛṣṭyāhi sādhu-praveśa-maṇḍala sādhu-vakṣya-sarvasattvān sādhu-vajra jaḥ.* Having recited this mantra, the deity will then descend and grant accomplishment; immediately, the sound of "Excellent! (*sādhu*) will be heard from within the maṇḍala.
Next, one should lead the disciple into the maṇḍala according to the ritual procedure. Having entered, one should bestow these verses of samaya, saying:
"Whether good or not good, whether concerning oneself or others—such speech should not be uttered. One should always utter words of praise, such as 'Excellent!
(sādhu), and thereby achieve the excellent accomplishment of vocal karma."
"Furthermore, he bestows this great vidyā-mantra, saying:

'Oṃ jina-vajra-hana-śāsana. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then instructs the disciple to remove the face-cloth and prostrate before the noble deities; the disciple should then form the Vajrasādhu mudrā to perform the rite of offering."
"This is called the Vajra Excellent Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

the practitioner, before an image of the Tathāgata, should with a mind of earnest concentration recite 'Sādhu sādhu' one hundred thousand times using the three vajra-actions; this person shall immediately attain Buddhahood and achieve vast accomplishments."

"If there are those who have not yet achieved [success] as described above, if they can recite this great vidyā-mantra of this very family even once, they shall likewise obtain praise, endearment, playful laughter, and joy, and even attain all methods of accomplishment and so forth."
"This is called the *Sarvasaṃtoṣa-vajra-vidhi*.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now also proclaim the great mantra of my own family within this great ritual manual of yours. If there be any practitioner who cultivates this rite, they shall obtain all empowerments and all wealth and happiness."
He then spoke the great mantra:

"Oṃ vajraratna viśvagā sarvaratha-saptakārakāviścaṇḍa-m va-vata-tatra. Furthermore, he explained the ritual procedure for this maṇḍala: First, one should draw the outer maṇḍala according to the rules;
within it, draw an eight-spoked wheel. In the center, place the Bodhisattva Vajraratnapāṇi, and in the positions of the eight spokes, place the eight World-Protecting Deities (Lokapālas).
First, the Sun Deity; second, the Moon Deity; third, Śakra Devendra; fourth, Vaiśravaṇa; fifth, the Earth Deity; sixth, the Water Deity; seventh, the Fire Deity; eighth, the Wind Deity.

Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then binds the Vajraratna mudrā and recites the syllable *vaṃ*. Having entered the maṇḍala and prostrated to the noble deities, he next forms the mudrā of invitation by slightly bending the tips of the index fingers of both hands like hooks, and recites this great vidyā-mantra of invitation:

“Oṃ sarvaśāparipūraka mahāvajraratnasūryāya he vāgvan muñca muñca vajradhara sādhaya he sarvavipralambhaparipūraka va vata traṃ. Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, if one perceives signs of light, one should know that the deity has descended and will grant accomplishment.
Thereafter, according to the ritual procedure, have the disciple form the vajra-gem fist (*vajraratnamuṣṭi*) and, holding a beautiful flower, enter the maṇḍala.
Having entered, bestow upon them this samaya verse:
"Among all gifts—of wealth, Dharma, and fearlessness— The gift of Dharma alone is supreme."
"Day by day, through deeds of virtue performed without fail, you shall attain the wisdom of Vajragarbha.

Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra—*Oṃ vyavahāra-vajra-han-tara*—the master then causes the disciple to remove the face-cloth. After the disciple has prostrated before the noble deities, the ācārya bestows the empowerment according to the ritual and confers the vajra-jewel. The disciple then forms the *ratna-samaya-muṣṭi-mudrā* (the jewel-triple-fist seal) as an offering.
"This is called the Vajraratna Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:
the practitioner should gaze upward at the sky and recite [the mantra] continuously for one year."

When one year has passed, all accomplishments, all wealth and happiness, and all offerings will spontaneously emerge from the sky; the practitioner will become equal to the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja, without any difference.

"Even if one has not yet accomplished what was described above, if one can recite this great mantra (*mahā-vidyā*) of this very family even once, one will likewise be able to perform summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*), binding (*bandhana*), or acts of endearment (*vaśīkaraṇa*); cause all beings to come or go; gather together wealth and treasures or distribute them as one pleases; cause the appearance of hidden treasures (*nidhi*) within the earth, as well as other objects such as gold, silver, pearls, *maṇi* gems, and various riches; and accomplish all methods for empowerment (*abhiṣeka*)."
"This is called the Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of All Aims.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Great Light addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now also proclaim within this great ritual manual of yours the Dharma of Vajra-Light. If there be a practitioner who cultivates this Dharma, that person shall obtain immeasurable light capable of universally illuminating all, and shall attain all lights."
He then spoke the Great Mantra:
"Oṃ vajrasūrya jyotirdhvaja sarvamārapramardana. Furthermore, he explained the ritual procedure for this maṇḍala: First, one should draw the outer maṇḍala according to the rules;
in its center, one should draw a sun-wheel maṇḍala, within which is placed the Bodhisattva Mahāprabha, holding the sun and moon in his hands.
Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then binds the Vajraprabhā mudrā, enters the maṇḍala, and performs the gazing with radiant light.
Having prostrated to the noble ones, one should form the mudrās according to the ritual and recite this mantra for invocation:

"Oṃ vajrasūrya-ma-pasvauḥ pīṅga-praseke jaḥ. Having recited this mantra, the deity descends and manifests the appearance of a sun and moon disk, in order to bestow all accomplishments and all prosperity.
Thereafter, have the disciple don yellow robes and cover his face with yellow silk; holding a torch in his hand to act as the Vajra Illumination, he enters the maṇḍala.
Having entered, he bestowed these verses of samādhi, saying:
"Day after day, in the presence of the Buddhas, Or before an image of Vajrapāṇi, One should constantly offer lamps; That person shall be freed from sleep."
"Furthermore, he confers this great vidyā, saying:
'Oṃ avighnata-makara svāhā. Having conferred this great vidyā, he then instructs the disciple to remove the face-cloth and prostrate before the noble ones."
Having performed the offering with the lamp-torches held [in hand], one exits the maṇḍala.
This is called the Vajrasūrya Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

The practitioner should gaze upward at the sun and recite the Great Illumination (mahāvidyā) of their respective family one hundred thousand times; this person will then obtain immeasurable majestic radiance, becoming no different from the Bodhisattva Vajraprabha.

"If there are those who have not yet achieved what has been described above, should they recite this great mantra of this very family even once, they will likewise increase all majestic splendor, and their actions will remain untainted;
furthermore, they will attain purity of mind and be able to give rise to the light of samādhi that illuminates all darkness of ignorance;
moreover, the disks of the sun and moon will appear in the sky, emitting great radiance."
Furthermore, he manifests a circular halo displaying various colors and forms, dispelling all darkness and illuminating his own body with light that pervades the entire world;
moreover, there is a blazing radiance shining forth—water emerging from the moon and fire emerging from the sun—until he finally gains entry into the Great Vajra Radiance Maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas.
"This is called the Ritual Manual of the Great Samaya, the Illusory Vajra Radiance.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Ratnaketu addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now bestow upon you, within this great ritual manual, the Dharma of the Invincible Banner. If there is a practitioner who cultivates this Dharma, that person shall be invincible amidst all hosts of māras, armies, and enemies; they shall obtain all manner of rare jewels, wealth, grain, and prosperity, which shall be inexhaustible."
He then spoke this great mantra:
“Oṃ aparājita-śrīkīrti sarva-śatru-pramardanī sarva-ratna-tejo-garbhā-yūre | jaya jaya | sarvama-sādhye hūṃ traṭ. Furthermore, he taught this maṇḍala ritual procedure:

In accordance with the ritual, one should draw the outer maṇḍala; within its center, one should measure out and construct a square maṇḍala according to the rite, surrounding it entirely with vajra-jeweled banners.
In the center, one should install the Bodhisattva Vajraratnaketu, who likewise holds a jeweled banner.
At each of the four cardinal directions and the four intermediate corners, one should place various exquisite jewels, diverse and extraordinary garments, ornaments, and other requisites.

Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms vajra-fists with both hands in the gesture of an erected jeweled banner. Having entered the maṇḍala, the ācārya’s heart trembles; he bows his head low in a gesture of reverence, and then raises his head again, reciting this mantra of invocation:

“Oṃ vajratvagarāgacā sarvatrātmapraṇamye svā viśaya viśaya siṃha sarvasaṃgarāmīvyuttarāntare. Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity will subsequently descend from the midst of space, manifesting various kinds of gold, jewels, wealth, clothing, ornaments, and other requisites; from that time forth, one shall constantly receive these offerings.
Thereafter, according to the ritual, the disciple is caused to enter the maṇḍala. Having entered, he is granted this samaya verse:
"This is the banner of all Buddhas, Symbolizing the loftiness and excellence of the pāramitās.
If this banner is placed within one's home, One shall attain supreme victory among all evil associates."
"Furthermore, he bestows this great vidyā-mantra, saying:
'Oṃ aparājita-vajra-ṣṭaḥ. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then instructs the disciple to remove the face-cloth and prostrate before the noble deities."
The ācārya bestows the precious banner, and the disciple immediately makes an offering with this banner.
"This is called the Supreme Banner Adornment Maṇḍala."
"Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed as follows:

the practitioner should establish the Vajra-Jewel Banner according to the ritual, and with focused contemplation, recite the mantra one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*). Once the accomplishment of the Jewel Banner is attained, one immediately obtains all forms of wealth, happiness, enjoyments, and requisites."
If there is anyone who grasps this precious banner, they shall become no different from the Bodhisattva Vajraratnaketu.

As previously stated, even for those who have not yet attained accomplishment, if they can recite the great mantra of this family once, they will likewise achieve the most excellent of all matters; they shall obtain all things such as pearls, maṇi jewels, clothing and ornaments, food and drink, and various riches.
"This is called the *Mahāsamaya-asamjaya-dhvaja-vidhi* (The Ritual Manual of the Great Samaya, the Invincible Banner).
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pramudita-indriya addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"I shall now bestow upon you within this great ritual manual the Dharma of Great Joy; if there be any practitioner who cultivates this Dharma, they shall always obtain joy at all times."
Then he spoke this great mantra:
"Oṃ ha ha ha ha (1) mahā-smitite (2) mahā-bhṛtikārike (3) hi hi hi hi (4). Furthermore, he taught the ritual procedure for this maṇḍala:
According to the rules, one should draw the outer maṇḍala, and in its center, construct a square maṇḍala whose shape is level and even, like the appearance of teeth.
In the center is seated the Bodhisattva Vajrarati, with his two hands forming the mudrā of joy;
in the four directions are seated four bodhisattvas—namely, Vajrapāṇi, Abhiṣekavajra, and so forth.
Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms the mudrā of joy, enters the maṇḍala, and prostrates to the noble deities.
Next, form the mudrā for summoning and recite this great mantra of invocation:

“Oṃ mahāhāsāya hi jaḥ | sarvamu[kha]praveśaya hūṃ | sarvavīradayini bandha bandha | sarvaharṣaṇasādya ho | ha ha ha ha hoḥ. Having recited this great mantra, the deity will then descend. Although no physical signs appear, the practitioner knows it within himself; his mind becomes greatly joyful, and from this, the accomplishment of the Dharma of Joy arises.
Thereafter, the disciple also forms the mudrā according to the ritual and next enters the maṇḍala while holding a flower.
Having entered, he is given this samaya verse:
"Within the two states of joy and anger, May there be neither enemy nor friend, neither suffering nor pleasure."
"Always open the eye of joy and proclaim joyful speech; Then one shall attain equality in all things.
He then conferred this great vidyā-mantra:

"Oṃ sarvāri-praṇāha. Having conferred this great vidyā-mantra, he then had the disciple remove the face-cloth and prostrate before the noble deities. He bestowed upon him joy, and the Vajra-disciple should form the Vajra-joy mudrā as an offering.
"This is called the Vajra-Ānanda Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

the practitioner should, according to the ritual procedures of this very dharma, assume a joyful countenance and perform recitation one hundred thousand times; thereafter, one shall attain the state of the Bodhisattva Ānandendriya."

"If there are those who have not yet achieved [success] as described above, if they can recite the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) of their respective family even once, they will likewise be able to give rise to all joy."
"This is the Ritual of the Great Samaya, Vajra-Ānanda.

who was granted the purple robe, together with others, by imperial decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ārya Avalokiteśvara addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
“I shall now also bestow upon you within this Great Ritual Manual the method of samādhi. Why is this?

Because by being able to visualize this samādhi, one can attain the great sovereign dharma of all Tathāgatas and become a Dharma King over all the three realms; even my own attainment of the name ‘Avalokiteśvara’ was established from within such a dharma.”

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara manifested a posture of loftiness; holding a lotus flower in his left hand and forming the *praphullita-mudrā* (the blooming-flower seal) with his right, he spoke this Great Mantra (*mahāvidyā*) for entering the *samādhi* gateway:
"Oṃ yathā-lokadhātūnām svāhā. "If one can contemplate and visualize this *mahāvidyā-samādhi* gateway according to the ritual rules, such a person will swiftly attain all accomplishments."
"Furthermore, the ritual procedure for this maṇḍala is explained:
one should draw the outer maṇḍala according to the rules;
in its center, one should draw an eight-petaled lotus, and place the Bodhisattva Vajranetra therein."
On the eight petals, one should place the eight Lotus-Holding Bodhisattvas, adorned with the physical characteristics and ornaments like those of Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva;
on the four outer corners, one should place Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and the Eleven-Faced Holy One.
Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms the Great Lotus Mudrā and enters the maṇḍala.
Having entered, he again forms the Invitation Mudrā and recites this great mantra of invitation: "Oṃ vajraniratrāvalokiteśvara."
Vaiśvāsika vajradharmasamādhi sarvajagattināṅkuru.

Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity will subsequently descend and, according to one's merit, manifest all manner of accomplishments and so forth.
Thereupon, the disciple first forms the Lotus Samādhi Fist and, holding a lotus, enters the maṇḍala.
Having entered, he is given this samaya verse:
"All intrinsic natures are pure; Whether sentient or insentient in the world,"
"In all places, the mind is always free from the dualistic marks of discrimination between defilement and purity.
Then, he bestowed this great vidyā-mantra:

"Oṃ aśuddhihana phaṭ. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then had the disciple remove the face-cloth. With a heart full of reverence for the worthy ones and the sages, the disciple placed the flower they held within the maṇḍala, and subsequently performed an offering by forming the *padma-samādhi-muṣṭi-mudrā*.
"This is called the Universal Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

the practitioner should create a painted image (*paṭa*), depicting Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva according to the rites of the root tantra, with the eight Tathāgatas and others painted to his left and right."

Having thus completed the painting, the practitioner forms the Great Lotus Mudrā before the painted image and visualizes the King of Samādhis. After one year of recitation and the completion of the ritual practice, they will attain mastery over all worlds and become indistinguishable from the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

"Even if one has not yet accomplished what has been described above, by merely entering this maṇḍala and reciting the great vidyā-mantra of the respective family once, one shall likewise attain all accomplishments, all wealth and happiness, full realization of all dharmas, and the ability to perform all deeds."
"This is called the Ritual Manual of the Sovereign of All Worlds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajracakra addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now bestow upon you within this Great Ritual Manual the entry into all dharma-gates. If there is anyone who can recite the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) of their own family even once, that person will be able to enter all maṇḍalas and attain the non-empty accomplishment of all dharmas."
Then he spoke this great mantra:
"Oṃ vajra-kīla hūṃ jaḥ. Furthermore, he taught this maṇḍala ritual: One should follow the previous maṇḍala method and further draw the Vajradhātu, the Vajracakra, and the Vajraratna;
within that wheel, one should draw the Bodhisattva *Cittotpādadharmacakrapravartana* and the four great bodhisattvas.

First, named Mahāvīra; second, named Sarvamudrādhipati; third, named Mahāsāmāyika; fourth, named Mahāsiddhādhipati—furthermore, in the four corners are established the four offering Bodhisattvas of Lāsyā, Mālā, Gītā, and Nṛtyā.
Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms the Vajracakrin mudrā, which revolves like lightning, and enters the maṇḍala.
Having entered, turn to the right and immediately rotate the aforementioned mudrā above the crown of the head.

After prostrating to the noble ones and sages, next form the hook with the index fingers of both hands to perform the Vajracakra-āhvāna-mudrā (the Invoking Seal of the Vajra Wheel), and recite this great mantra of invocation: *Oṃ vajrakarṣaya*.

*Sadhaya sarvasiddhiṃ huṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ.* (5) “Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā) subsequently descends.

That ācārya then abides having received the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the Great Vajra-ācārya; because he has first entered this ritual procedure (*vidhi*), he subsequently attains the state of a Great Vajra-ācārya.”
Thereafter, have the disciple likewise form the Vajra-Cakra Mudrā, hold a sublime flower with both hands, and enter the maṇḍala.
Having entered, bestow upon him this samaya verse:
"If one can [practice] daily, or for a month, Or even for the full duration of a year,"
"With supreme offerings according to one's capacity, One should worship the most excellent maṇḍala.
Then, he bestowed this great vidyā-mantra:

"Apraveśana HŪṂ. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then had the disciple remove the face-cloth, prostrate before the noble deities, and was given the Vajracakra-mudrā; using this mudrā, he then performed the offering.
"This is called the Vajracakra Maṇḍala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

the practitioner should construct the Vajracakra Maṇḍala, arranging it according to the ritual rules in whatever size he desires; having entered the maṇḍala, he should circumambulate before the image of the deity and remain there, reciting the great vidyā-mantra of his own family one hundred thousand times."

Once their meritorious practices are perfected, they shall attain the complete assembly of all supreme maṇḍalas; thereafter, they will become Vajradhara, or else they will become the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra who turns the wheel of Dharma upon the initial arousal of the mind of awakening.

Furthermore, if a practitioner can recite this great mantra of this very family even once, that person will immediately attain the fulfillment of all the secret mudrās of the Great Beings, all samādhis, all accomplishments, and all ritual activities.
"This is called the Ritual Procedure for Entering the Great Accomplishment Offering.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajradharma addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now proclaim within this great ritual procedure of yours the secret phrases of the True Dharma. If there are practitioners who cultivate this method, those persons will be able to accomplish all activities; furthermore, they will be able to pacify and eliminate all karmic burdens and achieve success, swiftly attaining fulfillment and remaining free from all demonic obstacles, even unto the attainment of the fruit of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
He then spoke the Great Mantra:
"Oṃ svabhāvaśuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ. Furthermore, he explained this maṇḍala ritual: According to the rite, one should draw the outer maṇḍala;
in its center, one should draw a great lotus wheel, and within that wheel, one should alone install the Bodhisattva Dharmacakra.

Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms the mudrā of Turning the Wheel of the True Dharma and places it upon his crown. He enters the maṇḍala, prostrates with his entire body to the ground before the noble deities, and forms the mudrā of invocation by slightly bending the tips of the joints of the index fingers of both hands like hooks. He then recites this great vidyā-mantra of invocation:

"Oṃ sarvadharmāśuddhatāgata svadharma jhaḥ hūṃ | īśaprativārito me | tiṣṭha sarvadharmaiḥ śuddhaya | sarvapāpavaraṇanāśaya aḥ ||" Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā) will then descend, enabling the ācārya to realize that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is primordially pure.
Thereafter, according to the ritual, the disciple is led into the maṇḍala by the ācārya in the same manner as the ācārya himself. Having entered, the following samaya verse is bestowed:
"That which is ever-present in all its aspects, This great dharma-phrase is the most supreme;
As the World-Honored Buddha has always taught, This dharma is the sound of Amoghasiddhi."
"Furthermore, he bestows this great vidyā, saying:
'Oṃ mara-krama' (1). Having bestowed this great vidyā, he then instructs the disciple to remove the face-cloth and prostrate before the noble ones."
Next, one should bestow the secret mantra of the True Dharma, and thereafter form the seal of the True Dharma to perform the offering.
This is called the Maṇḍala of the Wheel of the True Dharma.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed as follows:

The practitioner, according to the ritual, should draw the Maṇḍala of the True Dharma Wheel using colored powders as appropriate; in its center, he should install the principal deity, the Bodhisattva of the True Dharma Wheel, alone.

Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the practitioner enters the altar according to the ritual and performs recitation; without limiting the number of repetitions until the practice is perfected, one will, in this very life, become no different from the Bodhisattva Pravartadharmacakra.

"Even if one has not yet accomplished what was described above, if they can recite this great mantra of this very family even once, then all their karmic obstructions, bad dreams, evil omens, various fears, the suffering and distress of illness, craving, stinginess and envy, anger and resentment, arrogance, the affliction of malaria, possession by malevolent spirits, the constraints of seals and dhāraṇīs, alarm, confusion, battles, disputes, and all manner of evil harassments—even all unwholesome states such as greed, hatred, and delusion—shall be completely extinguished."
"This is called the Ritual Manual of the Vajra Wheel of the True Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrānabhilāpya addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now also bestow upon you within this great ritual manual the dharma-gate of recitation. If there is a practitioner who recites even once from within this dharma, that person shall immediately attain all accomplishments and fulfill all supreme activities."
He then spoke the Great Mantra: "Vā vā vā vā. Furthermore, he taught this maṇḍala ritual:
According to the rite, one should draw the outer maṇḍala and within it, the form of a four-sided maṇḍala; in its center, one should alone place the Bodhisattva Vajravācā holding a rosary.

Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then forms the *akṣamālā-mudrā* (rosary seal) and enters the maṇḍala. Placing his knees upon the ground, he pays homage to the noble ones (*āryas*). With the index finger of his left hand slightly bent like a hook and his right hand formed into a fist resting at his side, he performs the *āvāhana-mudrā* (invocation seal) and recites this great vidyā-mantra for invocation:
"Oṃ vajravāca ākhye siṃ vajra vajra jaḥ. Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) will then descend and bestow the method for accomplishing Vajra Speech.
Thereafter, according to the ritual, the disciple likewise forms the mudrā as before and enters the maṇḍala.
Having entered, the following samaya verse is bestowed:
"Recite this daily at the clear dawn; The great vidyā-mantra, completed one hundred and eight times."
"Having recited, there is neither grasping nor abandoning; the mind abides in the most supreme, true principle.
Then, he bestowed this great vidyā-mantra:

"Oṃ mūka-mardita-vajra. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then had the disciple remove the face-cloth, prostrate before the noble deities, and was given a rosary, after which he performed the offerings as before.
"This is called the *maṇḍala* of the True Recitation.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:

if the practitioner, according to the ritual, performs the mudrā of Vajra Speech before the image of the deity and recites for one year, once the practice is perfected, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi will immediately bestow all supreme accomplishments."

"If there are those who have not yet achieved [the results] as described above, if they can recite this Great Vidyā of this very family even once, all their undertakings shall likewise be accomplished according to their wishes."
"This is called the Ritual Manual of the Great Samaya of Silence.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajraviśvakarman addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now also bestow upon you, within this great ritual manual, the method for one's own *karma*. If there is a practitioner who cultivates this rite, all the activities they undertake will swiftly attain accomplishment."
He then spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
“Oṃ mahārata-viśikha siddhe nṛtyapūjya khage viśvavajra-sādhye sarvaṃ prasādaya vajranṛtyanṛtya-vaṅkura hūṃ vāgvaṃ vajrakarmā. Furthermore, he taught this maṇḍala ritual procedure:
In accordance with the ritual, one should draw the outer maṇḍala, and within it, draw the eight vajra maṇḍalas. In the center, place the Bodhisattva Vajraviśvakarman;

in its eight positions, place the eight venerable deities of offering: first, named Subhaga; second, named Vajrābhiṣeka; third, named Stuti; fourth, named Nṛtya; fifth, named Lāsya; sixth, named Hāsya; seventh, named Rasā; and eighth, named Kāla-pūjā.

Having thus arranged the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then binds the Lāsyā-vajra mudrā; taking a beautiful flower, he enters the maṇḍala and performs an offering by executing the gesture of the vajra dance with the upper part of his body.
Next, one should form the seal of invocation according to the ritual procedure and recite this great vidyā-mantra of invocation:
"Oṃ vajravisvāmukha-pratīhāra-cchinda karmaya he jjaḥ."

*Sadhaya sadhaya āḥ.* Having recited this great vidyā-mantra, the tutelary deity (iṣṭadevatā) will then descend, manifesting auspicious signs just as they appeared within the great maṇḍala previously described.
Thereafter, according to the ritual injunctions, the disciple likewise enters the maṇḍala with the same procedure as before. Having entered, the master imparts this samaya verse:
"Vajrapāṇi and all the other noble deities, Extend your filial devotion according to your capacity;
May the welfare of self and others be fully accomplished, And may offerings be presented daily."
"Furthermore, he bestows this great vidyā-mantra, saying:

'Oṃ hana vajrapuñjaka-riye ṇi ṇi' (1) 'Oṃ hana vajrapuñjaka-m' (2). Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then causes the disciple to remove the face-cloth and instructs him in the rites of offering and so forth."
"This is called the Vajra-karmamandala.
Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:
the practitioner should, according to the ritual, present various offerings before the image of the deity to the best of their ability, making offerings to the deity and all the Tathāgatas."

The practitioner further performs the secret offering rite of the Vajra Dance, reciting the mantra for one year as appropriate. Once the practice is perfected, they become indistinguishable from the Bodhisattva Vajraviśvakarman and further attain all the accomplishments of skillful arts bestowed by all Tathāgatas.
"If there are those who have not yet achieved success as described above, if they can recite this great mantra of the family even once, all their undertakings will also be swiftly accomplished."
"This is called the Unsurpassed Ritual Manual for All Karmas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāla addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now also explain for you, within this great ritual manual, the method for performing protection. If there are practitioners who cultivate this method of protection, they will attain invisibility even among all the Vajra families; how much more so would evil māras and the like dare to come and harass them?"
He then uttered the great vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ mahā-vajra-kavaca vajri-kuru sarvaṃ vajrāṅga. Furthermore, he taught this maṇḍala ritual procedure:
"In accordance with the dharma, one should draw the outer maṇḍala."
Within, draw the form of a four-sided maṇḍala; around its perimeter, further draw the vajra armor, which possesses a radiant appearance that manifests with dense brilliance.
In the center, install the Bodhisattva Vajrapāla; on the four sides, further install the four great bodhisattvas:
first, named Vajramukuṭa; second, named Vajrūrnakośa; third, named Vajradharma; and fourth, named Vajramuṣṭi.
Having thus laid out the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then binds the vajra-armour mudrā and enters the maṇḍala.

Having entered, he touches the crown of his head to the ground and pays homage to the noble deities. Next, with both hands, he slightly bends the index fingers into hooks to form the vajra-armour invocation mudrā and recites this great mantra of invocation: "Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānagatā."

the deity will subsequently descend; according to one's merit, one will immediately attain a body and life as firm and solid as vajra."
Thereafter, according to the ritual injunctions, the disciple binds the Vajra Armor mudrā and enters the maṇḍala while holding a beautiful flower.
Having entered, he is given this samaya verse:
"Amidst the two categories of enemies and kin, One should always practice firm and steadfast compassion with equanimity."
"May all protect this well-guarded one; you should constantly perform the work of protection.
Then, he bestowed this great vidyā-mantra:
"Oṃ sarvatrāsaya. Having bestowed this great vidyā-mantra, he then had the disciple remove the face-cloth and further bestowed this great vidyā-mantra for the adamantine armor that protects the body:

"Oṃ chliṃ. This great vidyā-mantra can completely exhaust the three realms, providing universal protection and attaining all forms of respect and affection; all maṇḍalas whatsoever employ this armor mantra for their offerings."
"Furthermore, the method for accomplishment is proclaimed:
If the practitioner recites the Armor Great Mantra according to the rite one hundred thousand times, they shall attain a firm body in this very life, free from aging and death."

"If there are those who have not yet accomplished what has been described above, should they recite this great mantra of the family even once, such a person can perform all vajra-activities; they shall protect the three vajra-actions by establishing the boundary and the maṇḍala boundary, and obtain all supreme armor-dharmas."
"This is called the Ritual Manual for the Supreme Protection of All.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvamārapramardin, by means of the Vajrayakṣa Dharma for converting through the skillful means of all Tathāgatas, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"I shall now bestow upon you within this great ritual manual the supreme method of subjugation. If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will be well able to subdue all evil māras and others; whatever subjugations they perform will swiftly attain accomplishment."
He then spoke the Great Mantra:
